title: General Rules of Succession in the Case of Female Hindus — Section 15 HSA

content.overview: Section 15 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 lays down the general rules of intestate succession to the property of a female Hindu. Property devolves firstly upon sons and daughters (including children of any pre-deceased son or daughter) and the husband; secondly upon the heirs of the husband; thirdly upon the mother and father; fourthly upon the heirs of the father; and lastly upon the heirs of the mother, with special rules in s. 15(2) for property inherited from parents or husband/father-in-law.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Female Hindu intestate? (2) Source of property (own / from parents / from husband)? (3) Apply s. 15(1) order or s. 15(2) special rule?
content.study:
Section 15(1) order: (a) sons and daughters (including the children of any pre-deceased son or daughter) and the husband; (b) heirs of the husband; (c) mother and father; (d) heirs of the father; (e) heirs of the mother.

Section 15(2): special rules — property inherited from father or mother devolves, in the absence of a son or daughter (including children of pre-deceased son or daughter), upon the heirs of the father; property inherited from husband or father-in-law devolves, in the absence of a son or daughter (including such children), upon the heirs of the husband.

Section 16 provides the order of succession and manner of distribution among heirs of a female Hindu.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: s. 15(1) general order
sections.body: Children and husband first; then husband’s heirs; parents; father’s heirs; mother’s heirs.

sections.heading: s. 15(2) source-based exceptions
sections.body: Property inherited from parents or from husband/father-in-law follows special reversion-style rules when there is no son or daughter (including issue of pre-deceased child).

sections.heading: Distribution
sections.body: Manner of distribution among the heirs is under s. 16.

sections.heading: Contrast with male scheme
sections.body: Male intestacy follows s. 8 Class I/II scheme; female intestacy follows s. 15.

sections.heading: Application tip
sections.body: Always ask how the female acquired the property before applying s. 15(1) or (2).

provisions.title: General rules of succession in the case of female Hindus

examples.title: Children and husband
examples.body: Female Hindu dies intestate leaving son, daughter and husband — they take under s. 15(1)(a).

examples.title: Property from father, no children
examples.body: Property inherited from father; no son or daughter — s. 15(2) points to heirs of the father.

hypotheticals.question: Why does source of property matter under s. 15?
hypotheticals.analysis: Because s. 15(2) displaces the general order when property was inherited from parents or husband/father-in-law and there is no son or daughter (including specified issue).

distinctions.title: s. 15 female vs s. 8 male intestacy

misconceptions.trap: Female intestacy uses the same Class I list as males under s. 8.
misconceptions.correction: Female intestacy is under s. 15, with a different order and source-based rules in s. 15(2).
